newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Megaworld, unit loans in order - C. Bank.
newsitem.headline: Megaworld, unit loans in order - C. Bank.

text.p: A senior Philippine Central Bank official said on Wednesday that outstanding bank loans of property firm Megaworld Properties & Holdings Inc and its unit Empire East Land Holdings Inc were in order.

"We've checked. And we didn't see any problem," Central Bank deputy governor Alberto Reyes told Reuters when asked whether the two companies had been reneging on their loan payments because of cashflow problems, which has been the subject of speculation in the stock market.
Reyes is the head of the supervision and examination sector of the Central Bank.
Megaworld has fallen to 3.50 pesos from 9.00 pesos since the start of the month, while Empire East has plunged to 3.65 pesos from 10.25 pesos on March 31.
Megaworld officials have denied persistent rumours about the financial health of it and its subsidiary Empire East.
It described as vicious and unfounded rumours on Tuesday that Empire East was about to declare bankruptcy.
Reyes said it was unlikely that Megaworld would be encountering financial problems, since its owners had recently decided to revive a foreclosed bank, Manila Banking Corp.
"There will not be a repeat of Victorias," Reyes said.
Victorias Milling Corp recently sought a 90-day debt payment moratorium due to its cashflow problem.
